title: The Bosphorus Brief — 25 August 2026
overview: A quiet news day carries two heavy items: the European Court of Human Rights is set to announce its decision in the long-running Kavala case, and new US sanctions on Iran are already rippling into conversations about Turkey's economy and region. Meanwhile, the lira holds steady and everyday residency and border news continues in the background.
body: The European Court of Human Rights is expected to announce its decision on the Kavala case today, a matter followed closely by both international outlets (BBC, DW, Euronews) and independent Turkish press (Medyascope, agos.com.tr). This is a case with implications for how Turkey's courts and rights protections are viewed abroad, and it sits alongside a separate story this week: five opposition mayors were sentenced to prison terms of up to 23 years, a decision opposition-leaning and international outlets describe as politically charged, while pro-government coverage has been largely silent on the framing. For foreign residents, these cases don't carry direct legal consequences, but they're worth watching as indicators of the broader rule-of-law climate.
